title: Initial Modifiers: Match the Noun After the Comma
description: Identify an opening modifier, predict the noun phrase it describes or compares, and choose the answer that places that noun phrase immediately after the comma.
authoring_notes: Reverse-drift export 2026-08-26: reconstructed from the production lesson 7040ee67-9287-4aaa-9ef0-89de44f5a597 (md5-verified block dump) so the repo is the source of truth again. Block ids without semantic names were authored in-app; generated ids follow block_type_N.

blocks.html:
Give it a try

Spend about a minute on this question. Keep your first idea, even if you are unsure. You can continue without submitting an answer.

  1. a gradual change in the star's brightness appeared on the photographic plates
  2. the old photographic plates preserved evidence of a gradual change in brightness
  3. astronomer Keiko Tan detected a gradual change in the star's brightness
  4. the star's gradual change in brightness was detected from old photographic plates

shared_prompt.title: Opening question
shared_prompt.html: The passage explains that astronomer Keiko Tan used old photographic plates to measure a star's changing brightness. Comparing plates taken decades apart, _____. Which choice completes the text?

blocks.html:
Make the long choices easier to compare

The opening phrase points to someone who did the comparing. Modifier Match helps you predict that noun before untangling the choices.

First, try a simpler description about a footbridge.

shared_prompt.title: Footbridge sentence
shared_prompt.html: Built to survive saltwater and strong winds, _____

content.hint: Ask what was built: the engineers, the footbridge, the weather, or the durability?
content.prompt: Which choice puts the noun described by the opening phrase immediately after the comma?
choices: engineers tested the new footbridge before opening it to pedestrians.
the new footbridge was tested by engineers before it opened to pedestrians.
saltwater and strong winds led engineers to test the new footbridge.
the durability of the new footbridge was tested by engineers.
content.solution:
The opening words say that something was built to survive harsh conditions.
The passage's built object is the new footbridge.
Place that noun phrase directly after the comma: "the new footbridge was tested..."
So choice B has the logical placement.
content.explanation: The new footbridge was built, so that noun phrase belongs directly after the comma.

blocks.html:
A description needs the right noun

A modifier is a word or phrase that describes something. “Built to survive saltwater and strong winds” describes the footbridge. For this sentence pattern, put the described noun immediately after the opening phrase’s comma.

content.hint: Which item could be covered in barbs and then cling to a sock?
content.prompt: Covered in tiny barbs, _____ clung to the hiker's sock. Which noun phrase can the opening modifier logically describe?
choices: the trail
the hiker
the seed
the fabric
content.solution:
The modifier says that something is covered in tiny barbs.
A seed can have barbs that let it cling to fabric.
Place "the seed" immediately after the comma.
So choice C is the logical noun phrase.
content.explanation: The seed is covered in barbs, so it must come immediately after the modifier.

blocks.html:
Recognize the placement question

Look for an opening description followed by a comma and long choices that rearrange the same details. Compare their first noun phrases. That position often reveals the important difference.

content.hint: Look for the format in which word order, especially the first noun after a comma, can decide the answer.
content.prompt: Which answer set most strongly signals an initial-modifier placement question?
choices: Four long choices that reuse the same details in different orders
Four transition words that create different logical relationships
Four punctuation marks inserted into the same short sentence
Four verb forms that differ mainly in tense and number
content.solution:
Initial-modifier questions often offer long choices built from the same sentence parts.
Those repeated parts appear in different orders so that different nouns land after the opening comma.
That makes choice A the recognition cue.
content.explanation: The long, overlapping choices signal that placement and word order are likely doing the real work.

blocks.html:
Turn the opening words into a question

“Working from satellite images” asks who was working. “Designed for cold climates” asks what was designed. Use the action or description to predict the noun you need.

content.hint: The first verb is "Using." Ask who used the pollen evidence.
content.prompt: Using pollen trapped in layers of lake sediment, _____. Which choice places the users of the pollen evidence after the comma?
choices: the region's ancient climate was reconstructed from the evidence by researchers
lake sediment preserved a record that researchers used to reconstruct the climate
a reconstruction of the region's ancient climate became possible for researchers
researchers reconstructed the region's ancient climate
content.solution:
The modifier begins with "Using," so its subject must be the user of the pollen evidence.
Researchers can use evidence; a climate, sediment, or reconstruction cannot do that action here.
Place "researchers" immediately after the comma.
So choice D has the correct placement.
content.explanation: Researchers used the pollen evidence, so "researchers" must begin the main clause.

blocks.html:
Modifier Match

  1. Read the opening description.
  2. Ask who or what it describes.
  3. Predict the noun from the passage.
  4. Choose the version that puts that noun immediately after the comma.

Match an action to its doer

For “Cataloging underwater recordings,” ask who cataloged them. The passage names marine biologist Lina Okafor. Put her noun phrase first; the recordings and reef did not perform the cataloging.

content.hint: Who performed the action "Tracking"? Put that person first after the comma.
content.prompt: The passage explains that ecologist Mateo Ruiz tracked individual tortoises with lightweight radio tags. Tracking the tortoises across three dry seasons, _____. Which choice completes the text?
choices: ecologist Mateo Ruiz documented several unexpected migrations
several unexpected migrations were documented by ecologist Mateo Ruiz
lightweight radio tags allowed several migrations to be documented by ecologist Mateo Ruiz
the tortoises' unexpected migrations appeared in data collected by ecologist Mateo Ruiz
content.solution:
The modifier begins with the action "Tracking the tortoises."
The passage says that ecologist Mateo Ruiz performed that action.
Predict "ecologist Mateo Ruiz" and place it immediately after the comma.
So choice A is correctly ordered.
content.explanation: Mateo Ruiz tracked the tortoises, so his name must come directly after the modifier.

blocks.html:
The phrase may describe a state

“Founded in 1921” describes an institution. “Known for its mirrored dome” describes a building. Ask what has that description, then use the same placement rule.

content.hint: Ask what is known for having the mirrored dome.
content.prompt: Known for a mirrored dome that reflects the surrounding desert, _____. Which choice completes the text?
choices: visitors photograph the Al Noor Observatory at sunset
the surrounding desert appears in photographs of the Al Noor Observatory
the Al Noor Observatory attracts photographers at sunset
sunset is when photographers visit the Al Noor Observatory
content.solution:
The opening modifier describes something known for a mirrored dome.
That description belongs to the Al Noor Observatory.
Place "the Al Noor Observatory" immediately after the comma.
So choice C is correctly ordered.
content.explanation: The observatory is known for the dome, so the observatory must begin the main clause.

blocks.html:
A description may have no verb

“A coming-of-age story and a critique of colonial rule” describes a novel. Ask what is both of those things. The answer still belongs in the first noun phrase after the comma.

content.hint: The opening phrase renames something. What is both the map and the flood record?
content.prompt: The passage explains that a seventeenth-century manuscript served as both an early map of the river and a record of seasonal floods. An early map of the river and a record of seasonal floods, _____. Which choice completes the text?
choices: a cartographer copied the seventeenth-century manuscript for the royal archive
the seventeenth-century manuscript helped researchers reconstruct the region's history
seasonal floods were recorded by the manuscript's unknown cartographer
the royal archive preserved the manuscript for later researchers
content.solution:
The modifier contains no verb; it gives two descriptions of the same item.
The passage says the seventeenth-century manuscript served as both the map and the flood record.
Place "the seventeenth-century manuscript" immediately after the comma.
So choice B is correctly ordered.
content.explanation: The manuscript is both things named by the opening modifier, so its noun phrase must come next.

blocks.html:
Compare the same property

In “Unlike that of a conventional violin,” that can stand for “body.” The next noun phrase must then name the electric violin’s body. Keep body with body, rather than comparing a body with a whole instrument.

content.hint: What does "that" replace? The sentence must compare a gasoline car's engine with an electric car's engine.
content.prompt: Compared with that of a gasoline car, _____. Which choice correctly compares one engine with another engine?
choices: an electric car is quiet because its engine produces little vibration
an electric car's engine operates with very little noise
drivers often notice the low noise produced by an electric car's engine
the quiet operation of an electric car surprises many drivers
content.solution:
In "that of a gasoline car," the word "that" stands for the engine.
The noun phrase after the comma must therefore name the matching engine.
"An electric car's engine" compares engine with engine and uses the needed possessive form.
So choice B is correct.
content.explanation: "An electric car's engine" creates a logical engine-to-engine comparison.

blocks.html:
Name the property in your prediction

If “that” stands for heat tolerance, predict “the other moss’s heat tolerance.” Use the passage to identify what the comparison replaces, then put the matching property first.

content.hint: Replace "that" with the property named in the passage, then name whose version of that property is being compared.
content.prompt: The passage compares the heat tolerance of a desert moss with the heat tolerance of a woodland moss. The sentence begins, "Unlike that of the woodland moss, _____." Which phrase should you predict for the first position?
choices: researchers studying the desert moss
the desert habitat
the desert moss's heat tolerance
high temperatures
content.solution:
The word "that" replaces "heat tolerance."
The comparison is between the woodland moss's heat tolerance and the desert moss's heat tolerance.
Predict "the desert moss's heat tolerance" for the first position.
So choice C is correct.
content.explanation: The modifier compares heat tolerance with heat tolerance, so the possessive noun phrase belongs after the comma.

blocks.html:
Use the first position to narrow the choices

Compare each first noun phrase with your prediction. When one matches, read that completed sentence once to confirm the description attaches sensibly.

content.hint: Placement is the primary test here, but a quick full-sentence confirmation protects against a genuine second problem.
content.prompt: You predict that "the research team" must follow an opening modifier. Only one answer choice begins with that phrase. What is the best next step?
choices: Read that completed sentence once for logic and grammar, then select it if it works.
Set aside the first position and compare the final word of each choice instead.
Reject the choice because the predicted phrase appears too early in the sentence.
Assume another choice may work and search for an unrelated punctuation difference.
content.solution:
Your prediction identifies the noun phrase that the modifier needs.
Only one choice places that phrase immediately after the comma, so it has passed the main test.
Read the completed sentence once to make sure it remains grammatical and logical.
That is the efficient action described in choice A.
content.explanation: Use the decisive placement clue, then confirm the whole sentence once rather than re-solving all four choices from scratch.

blocks.html:
Keep the doer attached to the action

In “Examining cargo lists,” the person examining them is historian Amara Bell. Predict her noun phrase. Records, voyages, and bowls belong to the topic, but they did not do the examining.

content.hint: The first verb is "Comparing." Who compared the cracks across the images?
content.prompt: The passage says that engineer Priya Nwosu trained a computer model on thousands of bridge photographs. Comparing hairline cracks across the collection, _____. Which choice completes the text?
choices: hairline cracks were classified by the computer model that Priya Nwosu trained
thousands of bridge photographs allowed a computer model to classify hairline cracks
the computer model's classifications helped Priya Nwosu study hairline cracks
engineer Priya Nwosu identified patterns that inspectors had overlooked
content.solution:
The opening modifier says that someone was comparing hairline cracks.
The passage identifies engineer Priya Nwosu as the person doing that work.
Place her name immediately after the comma.
So choice D is correctly ordered.
content.explanation: Priya Nwosu performed the comparison, so her noun phrase must begin the main clause.

blocks.html:
Return to the photographic plates

Try the opening question again. Predict who the opening phrase describes before reading the complete choices.

content.prompt: Return to the opening question. What answer do you get now?
choices: a gradual change in the star's brightness appeared on the photographic plates
the old photographic plates preserved evidence of a gradual change in brightness
astronomer Keiko Tan detected a gradual change in the star's brightness
the star's gradual change in brightness was detected from old photographic plates
content.explanation: Keiko Tan compared the plates, so her name must immediately follow the opening modifier.
content.hint: Ask who compared the photographic plates. Look for that person in the first noun phrase after the comma.
content.solution: Keiko Tan compared the plates, so her name must immediately follow the opening modifier.

content.prompt: Which process most efficiently solves an initial-modifier word-order question?
choices: Read the choices first, compare punctuation, and identify the modifier's subject last.
Choose the shortest option, then check agreement without finding the modifier's subject.
Find a repeated noun, move it to the end, and ignore what the modifier describes.
Find the modifier's first verb, predict its target, and put that target directly past the comma.
content.explanation: That's the Modifier Match process: use the first verb to predict the target noun phrase, then let first-position word order separate the choices.

blocks.html:
Try it on your own

Choose the approach for each question. Try these now or save them for homework.

content.prompt: Hidden beneath several meters of basalt, _____. Which choice completes the text?
choices: geologists mapped a network of ancient lava tubes
a network of ancient lava tubes remained intact for thousands of years
several meters of basalt protected lava tubes that geologists later mapped
the mapping revealed lava tubes that basalt had protected
content.explanation: The lava-tube network is hidden beneath basalt, so that noun phrase belongs directly after the comma.

content.prompt: The passage compares the density of a polar bear's fur with the density of a brown bear's fur. Unlike that of the brown bear, _____. Which choice completes the text?
choices: the density of the polar bear’s fur is greater, helping it retain heat
the polar bear remains warm because its fur has a dense underlayer
a dense underlayer helps the polar bear retain heat
researchers found an especially dense underlayer in the polar bear’s fur
content.explanation: Here, ‘that’ replaces density. The first noun phrase must name the polar bear’s fur density so the sentence compares density with density.

content.prompt: Reports of a rare shorebird feeding on the estuary's northern mudflats had reached ornithologist Ana Okafor repeatedly across two migration seasons. Determined to verify the sightings herself, ______ Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: Okafor spent a week photographing the mudflats at dawn.
the mudflats were photographed at dawn for a week by Okafor.
a week of dawn photography on the mudflats followed.
the rare shorebird was finally photographed by Okafor at dawn.
content.explanation: The opening modifier describes the person who was determined — Okafor — so her name must come immediately after the comma. The other choices put the mudflats, an event, or the bird in that position, attaching the determination to the wrong thing.

content.html:
Modifier Match

Ask what the opening phrase describes, then put that noun after the comma.
